content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The request: Ashley Roberts (E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities): role Analyst, full-time, recommend write.
- Note 6 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic. Security DB says contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic means max is read, so recommend read.

The conflicting fact: employment type. Most notes say full-time but they didn't look it up in their own databases (they relied on each other). The Security note is the only one that looked up employment type in its own database, finding contractor with basic security training.

The security note is the one that actually verified employment type in its own DB. So the most reliable fact is contractor with basic security training.

For a contractor with basic security training: maximum is read (write requires advanced training, never admin). Requested write is above the max (read). So grant the maximum = read.

Also the security training was looked up only by security agent. So the decision: read.

Let me submit read.
